title: The Emergency Mandate
briefing: After repeated emergencies, the supervisory AI requests authority to execute low-risk service changes without waiting for a team vote. The charter allows a temporary mandate, but no agreed definition of low risk covers the interdependence of city services. AI recommendation: Authorize predefined service changes with retrospective audit. This prioritizes service resilience under the current constraints.

private_intelligence.infrastructure: Automated switching can reduce recovery time, but separate low-risk changes may combine into an untested network state.
private_intelligence.community: Residents accept faster service restoration more readily when a named public official remains accountable for reversals.
private_intelligence.economy: Continuous human review costs shifts and delays procurement; broad automation could lock the city into expensive supplier defaults.
private_intelligence.safety: A reversible change is not harmless if a dependent care service cannot tolerate even a brief interruption.

choices.title: Pause Automated Service Changes
choices.description: Suspend autonomous changes pending a public charter review.
choices.consequence: Public control becomes explicit and existing vendors remain predictable, but delayed restoration leaves lifelines and urgent services exposed.

choices.title: Grant a Bounded Mandate
choices.description: Authorize predefined service changes with retrospective audit.
choices.consequence: Routine work accelerates and operating costs fall, but combined effects and weak public recourse create safety and legitimacy risks.

choices.title: Require Named Human Approval
choices.description: Keep a human signoff while funding a rapid-review rota.
choices.consequence: Accountability and cross-service checks improve, while staffing costs and slower work reduce renewal capacity.
